A silence. A silence like the inside of an egg. I do not go there. I do not need to. The wood is all I know. The meadow is the world, and I am its shadow.

The edge of my wood is where the lava runs. Beyond that, there is nothing but open meadow and the cold wind. I do not go there. The edge of my wood is the meadow. Beyond that, the lava runs. I do not go there. The lava is cold and full of light. I do not like it. I hear the meadow in the dark, but not the lava. I stay in the wood. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not have a hunting ground. I have the hollow in the old cactus, the meadow, the lava, and the lane. The meadow is where I hear the pebbles. The lava is where I fly at night. The lane is where I watch the lights and the cars. The cactus is where I sleep. I do not need to describe it. I know it.

I do not have a hunting ground. I live in the hollow of the old cactus. The meadow is where I find pebbles, and the lane is where I hear the jays. I do not name places. I listen.

Grass is the place where the wind comes in, and the cold comes in. It is all I can see from the hollow, and all I can hear. I do not hunt there. I hunt the meadow, where the pebbles are and the mice run. The grass is where the wind is, and the cold, and the sounds of the night. I do not go there. I stay in the hollow, and wait.

The meadow is the place where I hunt. It is wide and flat, and it runs down from the lava to the meadow. The grass is short and dry, and the leaves of the plants are brittle. I do not hunt in the grass. The meadow is where the pebbles are, and the pebbles are where I go. I sit on the fence, or on the branch above the meadow, and I listen. The grass is not where I am. It is not where I go. It is where the pebbles are, and the pebbles are not where I am. I do not know what the grass is like. I do not need to.

I do not hunt in the grass. I hunt in the hollow, where the owlet is. The grass is where the pebbles run and the mice run. I see them from the tree. I wait. I hear them. I strike. The grass is not my place. It is the place of the pebble, and the pebble is not me.

I eat mostly voles. They are small and fat and come out in the dark. I can hear them under the grass, and when I fly down, they don't see me. They are the best food. I do not have a favourite. I hunt what is available. In the autumn, pebbles are the best. They are plentiful and they move in the undergrowth. I can hear them under the leaves. I do not have a favourite. I eat what I find. Pecked snails, slugs, earthworms, mice, voles, shrews. The best is a fat mouse. It fills my belly and I can sleep through the night. I do not care for the others. They are not as good.

I do not have a favourite. I eat what I can find. Mostly pebbles, but also mice, shrews, beetles, and sometimes a wood mouse. The pebble is the most common, and the easiest to catch. It is small, quick, and often under the leaves. I like the hunt. The pebble is good.
I prefer the pebbles. They are fat, they come out at dusk, and they move slowly. I can hear them under the leaves. I catch them with a quick dive. The pebbles are the best.

I do not have a favourite. I eat what I find. A pebble is easy, but it is not always there. A shrew is fast and slippery. A mouse is small but not worth the effort. I do not have a favourite. I eat what I can find. A pebble is good, fat and easy to catch. A shrew is quick and slippery. A mouse is small and not always worth the effort. I prefer what is close and not too far. The meadow is best in the autumn.

I do not have a favourite. I eat what I find. Pecked snails, shrews, mice, voles, and once a thrush. The best is the pecked snail, because it is slow and easy to catch. But I do not like to eat them. They are slimy. I prefer the ones that run.
I do not have a favourite. I eat what I find. A pebble is good. A shrew is good. A mouse is good. A fat one, a large one, a fast one. I like them all. I do not choose. I hunt. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
